node.title: Primitive shift-pair dyadic norm router
node.statement: For a disjoint equal-size shift pair on a dyadic multiplicative coset with equal first t locator coefficients, every allowed dyadic fold beta_j vanishes modulo the row field at the odd frequencies supplied by the prefix. If beta_j is nonzero, one residue-degree factor p^ord_n(p) divides its cyclotomic norm for every distinct Frobenius orbit reached; the orbit-weighted exponent is at least the number M_j of distinct available odd frequencies, while |Norm(beta_j)|<=E_j^(n/4) and E_j<=2^(j+2)e. The root fold beta_0 vanishes exactly on the common antipodal coefficient-scale branch, so every coefficient-primitive pair is canonically norm-gated. This is a necessary arithmetic router, not a population bound.
